text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- ELECTRICAL ENERGY SHARES ROSE MOST IN 1996
Shares of electrical energy companies, boosted by bright privatization prospects, rose most on Brazilian stock markets in 1996, surpassing even strongly rising telecommunications stocks.
-- US PRESSURES BRAZIL IN WTO ON AUTOMOBILE RULES
The United States on Friday sought new formal consultations before the World Trade Organization on Brazil's car import regime.
-- PMDB PARTY VOTES AGAINST RE-ELECTION

The PMDB, the largest party in Brazil's Congress, handed President Fernando Henrique Cardoso one of his biggest political defeats by voting against a constitutional amendment that would allow him to stand for re-election in 1998.
-- BOLSAS EXPECTED TO OPEN DOWNWARD ON NEW CPMF TAX

Brazilian stock markets are expected to slide today, led by foreign investor selling, in reaction to the government's decision last week to only partially exempt foreign capital from the new 0.2 percent CPMF tax on financial transactions.
O GLOBO
-- PMDB REBELS AND COMPLICATES RE-ELECTION DRIVE

The biggest party in Congress, the PMDB, decided Sunday not to vote until February 15 on a proposal that would let President Fernando Henrique Cardoso run for re-election, leaving party members free to make up their own minds on the issue.
-- TRADE MINISTER REACTS TO US PRESSURE ON CARS
Trade and Industry Minister Francisco Dornelles said he considers the United States' request for new consultations before the World Trade Organization on Brazil's auto import rules blackmail.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- PMDB PARTY CONVENTION REJECTS RE-ELECTION

The PMDB party's one-day convention handed President Fernando Henrique Cardoso a defeat by approving a recommendation against re-election and voting to delay a congressional vote on the issue until after February 15.
-- LANDLESS ARE MET WITH GUNFIRE AT SAO PAULO RANCH
Close to 300 landless farmers were fired on by security guards when they triedto squat on land belonging to the Santa Rita ranch in Sao Paulo's Mirante do Paranapanema area.
-- SAO PAULO DRUG TRAFFICKERS TO HAVE PROPERTY CONFISCATED
Sao Paulo state, in an effort to combat growing organized crime, plans to seize the property of drug traffickers who are arrested.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- James Craig, Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 232 4411
